## Unified API

Send operation input as a JSON object to `POST /api/v1/integrations/calendar/{operation}`. Use `Content-Type: application/json` and `Authorization: Bearer zint_...` with your app token. The token is scoped to one connection and category.

Read `GET /api/v1/integrations/calendar/capabilities` with the same token. It returns an object keyed by operation, each containing `support` and a `fields` map. It does not use the operation response envelope.

Successful operations return HTTP 200 with `{support, warnings, data}`. `support` is `native` or `emulated`. `warnings` is an array of `{code, field}` objects, empty when nothing was dropped. `data` has the operation's response fields below. Unknown input fields are rejected.

| Operation | Summary | Provider support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_event` | Create an event. | CalDAV: native; Google Calendar: native |
| `delete_event` | Delete an event. | CalDAV: native; Google Calendar: native |
| `free_busy` | Find busy intervals across calendars. | CalDAV: emulated; Google Calendar: native |
| `get_event` | Read one event. | CalDAV: native; Google Calendar: native |
| `list_calendars` | List the calendars you can access. | CalDAV: native; Google Calendar: native |
| `list_events` | List expanded events in a time window. | CalDAV: native; Google Calendar: native |
| `update_event` | Replace an event. | CalDAV: native; Google Calendar: native |

### `create_event`

Create an event.

Input fields:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attendees` | array of object | No | Attendees; omitted by providers without attendee support. |
| `attendees[].email` | string | No | Attendee email address. |
| `attendees[].name` | string | No | Attendee display name. |
| `attendees[].response` | string | No | Attendance response supplied by the provider. |
| `calendar_id` | string | Yes | Calendar identifier returned by list_calendars. |
| `description` | string | No | Event description; defaults to empty. |
| `end` | object | Yes | Exclusive end; must follow start and use the same time form. |
| `end.date` | string | Conditional | All-day date in YYYY-MM-DD form; excludes date_time. |
| `end.date_time` | string | Conditional | RFC 3339 instant with offset; excludes date. |
| `idempotency_key` | string | No | Stable key used to derive the event ID for repeat creates. |
| `location` | string | No | Event location; defaults to empty. |
| `start` | object | Yes | Start time. Set exactly one of date or date_time. |
| `start.date` | string | Conditional | All-day date in YYYY-MM-DD form; excludes date_time. |
| `start.date_time` | string | Conditional | RFC 3339 instant with offset; excludes date. |
| `title` | string | No | Event title; defaults to empty. |
| `transparent` | boolean | No | Whether the event leaves you available; defaults to false. |

### `delete_event`

Delete an event.

Input fields:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `calendar_id` | string | Yes | Calendar identifier returned by list_calendars. |
| `id` | string | Yes | Event identifier returned by list_events. |

Response fields in `data`:

An empty object (`{}`).

### `free_busy`

Find busy intervals across calendars.

Input fields:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `calendar_ids` | array of string | Yes | Between 1 and 50 non-empty calendar identifiers. |
| `from` | string | Conditional | Window start in RFC 3339. Required for list_events, free_busy, and emulated get_event. |
| `to` | string | Conditional | Window end in RFC 3339; after from and at most 366 days later. Required when from is required. |

Response fields in `data`:

| Name | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `calendars` | object mapping strings to array of object |
| `calendars.*.end` | string |
| `calendars.*.start` | string |

### Run a request

Set your app token before running this example.

```bash
export INTEGRATIONS_URL='https://app.zenith.hosting/api/v1/integrations'
read -r -s -p 'App token: ' CALENDAR_TOKEN
printf '\n'
export CALENDAR_TOKEN
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  "$INTEGRATIONS_URL/calendar/capabilities" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALENDAR_TOKEN"
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  "$INTEGRATIONS_URL/calendar/list_calendars" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALENDAR_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{}'
```

### Errors and strict mode

Integration errors return `{code, operation, provider}` with optional `field`, `message`, and `retry_after`. Authentication failures return only `{"code":"unauthorized"}` and a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header. Handle errors by `code`.

| Code | HTTP status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field_unsupported` | 422 | Strict mode rejected an unsupported input field before calling the provider. |
| `invalid_input` | 400 | Invalid JSON, fields, values, or degradation mode. |
| `not_found` | 404 | The requested resource was not found. |
| `operation_emulated` | 501 | Strict mode rejected an emulated operation. |
| `operation_unsupported` | 501 | The provider does not support this operation. |
| `provider_auth` | 424 | Provider credentials failed; reconnect the provider. |
| `provider_rate_limited` | 429 | Provider rate limit reached; respect the Retry-After header when present. |
| `provider_unavailable` | 502 | Provider failure or invalid response; retry later. |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | Missing, expired, revoked, or incorrectly scoped app token. |

Omit `Zenith-Degrade` or set it to `best-effort` to allow emulation. Dropped input fields produce `field_dropped` warnings. Send `Zenith-Degrade: strict` to reject emulation and unsupported input fields before the provider call. Unsupported operations fail in both modes.

## Provider support

`native` calls the provider directly. `emulated` combines native operations. `unsupported` cannot run. Support describes the adapter; provider permissions and resource availability still apply.

| Operation | CalDAV | Google Calendar |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_event` | native | native |
| `delete_event` | native | native |
| `free_busy` | emulated | native |
| `get_event` | native | native |
| `list_calendars` | native | native |
| `list_events` | native | native |
| `update_event` | native | native |

### Field support

These fields have explicit capability declarations. Check them before relying on invitations, labels, or pagination. Unsupported input fields are dropped in best-effort mode; field support on read operations also describes what the provider can return.

| Operation | Field | CalDAV | Google Calendar |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `create_event` | `attendees` | unsupported | native |
| `get_event` | `attendees` | unsupported | native |
| `list_calendars` | `page_token` | unsupported | native |
| `list_events` | `attendees` | unsupported | native |
| `list_events` | `page_token` | unsupported | native |
| `update_event` | `attendees` | unsupported | native |

## Setup

<Visibility for="humans">

<Steps>
<Step title="Connect a provider">
Open [Settings > Integrations](https://app.zenith.hosting/settings/integrations) in the Zenith dashboard. Choose a provider and enter its connection fields below.
</Step>
<Step title="Create an app token">
Create a token for your app on that connection. Copy it into the app's token input in the deployment Credentials panel.
</Step>
</Steps>

</Visibility>

Connection fields:

### CalDAV

| Field | Label | Required | Secret |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | URL | Yes | No |
| `username` | Username | Yes | No |
| `password` | Password | Yes | Yes |

### Google Calendar

| Field | Label | Required | Secret |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `access_token` | Access token | Yes | Yes |

### Declare app environment inputs

Merge this declaration into `zenith-compose.yml`. Replace `app` with the service that calls the API. See the [environment reference](/content/zenith-compose-reference#env).

```yaml zenith-compose.yml
x-zenith:
  env:
    INTEGRATIONS_URL:
      input:
        label: Integrations URL
        default: https://app.zenith.hosting/api/v1/integrations
      services:
        - app
    CALENDAR_TOKEN:
      input:
        label: Calendar token
        secret: true
      services:
        - app
```

The token has no default. Leave `input.required` unset so submission validation can run before the owner supplies it. Your app must handle a missing token and enable the integration after the owner configures it. These inputs use the published runtime contract; the current CLI preview policy does not accept `x-zenith.env`. For an authorized preview, follow the preview guide's local environment workflow and report any validation limit.

Copy this prompt into your coding agent.

```text Agent prompt
Connect this app to Zenith's calendar integration.

Install the Zenith skills from the app repository:
npx skills add zenith-hosting/skills

Read https://docs.zenith.hosting/content/integrations/calendar.md.
If zenith-compose.yml is missing, use zenith-setup and
zenith-compose, run NO_COLOR=1 zenith init, and adapt the
generated files to this app.
Then use the zenith-integrations skill to wire the app to the
category API. Declare INTEGRATIONS_URL and a secret CALENDAR_TOKEN
input for the calling service.
Read GET $INTEGRATIONS_URL/calendar/capabilities with the app
bearer token and choose features from operation and field
support; never hard-code a provider.
Call POST $INTEGRATIONS_URL/calendar/{operation} with JSON input.
Handle support, field_dropped warnings, typed errors,
Retry-After and a missing token. Send Zenith-Degrade: strict
when a dropped field or emulation would be incorrect.
Run the app's tests and NO_COLOR=1 zenith check after Compose
changes. Report preview-policy limits separately from
published runtime support.
With an authorized preview and token, verify a native and an
emulated operation where available, strict rejection and
visible warnings. Check side effects of authorized writes and
report anything unverified.
Do not invent tokens, log secrets, connect accounts, deploy or
publish without authorization for that action.
```

<Visibility for="agents">

Use the prompt above as the task contract. Report the commands run, observed results, and any checks blocked by missing credentials or unavailable dashboard setup. Passing local tests does not prove a live integration.

</Visibility>
